# Independent audit: four compatible roofs and the concave-profile obstruction

Audited `candidate c5a29d6b8953c3ed` in full, including the added moving-apex and signed K-only paragraphs. **PASS.** The obstruction is correctly limited to the displayed incidence, numerical weights, and profile conditions. Its polygon construction realizes the incidence and face geometry, but does not claim those weights are its actual section weights or that its caps are genuinely critical.

## 1. Compatible roofs and four-corner minimization

For q_L in [a,a0] and q_R in [b0,b], both ramps are nonnegative on I0 and at least one on J, so the minimum profile is nonnegative on I0 and exactly one on J. The finite-vertex compatibility proof from the signed-roof source applies: old midpoint vertices away from I0 and new seed vertices away from J have a fixed negative limiting normal height, while the face and seed points satisfy the new inequalities exactly. Unchanged K facets retain their strict slack on the new seed. Uniform boundedness, convergence, and the O(e^2) polygon corner correction are justified as in the independently audited companion source.

On [a,c], the left ramp is always the minimum branch; on [d,b] the right ramp is always the minimum branch. The plateau term is independent of the two parameters. Differentiation gives exactly the two signed numerators in (5)--(6). The denominators remain strictly positive on the compact parameter intervals. Hence each side cost is monotone or constant independently of the other, and one of four corners minimizes the menu cost. Point plateaus and degenerate parameter intervals cause no problem. Total-mass and endpoint conditions are not optimized by that argument and remain explicitly required.

## 2. Exact signed-measure inequality

The stated numbers obey Z-L=51/100 and Z+L=259/255. With A_*=7/100, direct integration gives total mass m=7/5000 and first moment 63/50000=mc, c=9/10>Z. The chosen weights give f=-7/100 on the two singleton regions and +7/100 on the pair region, with the stated numerical gauge bounds.

The signed measure nu=f ds-m delta_c has zero mass and first moment. Its positive part lies inside (L,Z), and its negative part lies outside [L,Z], including the negative atom at c. For any finite concave G, its difference from the affine chord through L,Z is nonnegative inside and nonpositive outside. Thus the product with nu is nonnegative. The affine chord integrates to zero against nu, proving the inequality integral G f>=mG(c) exactly. Endpoint conventions do not affect the Lebesgue terms, and the atom has the correct sign and location.

Every full-face tent is positive at c, so all its costs are strictly positive. The A face has twice the parameter length of I0; its unit-height tent integrates to |I0|, giving C_A=-7/50000. A required seed height G(c)>=1 therefore yields the exact positive total bound 7/12500. The affine constant roof realizes equality, so this is the exact infimum within the stated unconstrained concave-profile class.

## 3. Moving the apex and signed K-only variations

If c'>=c, concavity between a0 and c' gives G(c)>=(c-a0)/(c'-a0); if c'<=c, use b0 instead. Both coefficients exceed 1/2 for an interior c', and both equal one at c'=c. This gives the strict uniform cost bound 21/100000. The corresponding affine roof is nonnegative on all I0, has value one at c', and makes the signed-measure inequality an equality. Taking c' toward the appropriate face endpoint gives the stated exact infimum. Each fixed interior c' has its own valid small geometric variation, so no simultaneous limiting body/source argument is needed for this positive lower bound.

The finite-vertex compatibility proof also works for each of these affine roofs: its normal approaches the old facet normal, the old face stays below its nonnegative profile, the seed has the required height, and all other finite vertices retain fixed limiting slack. For a K-only signed roof with G>=0 on I0, the same inequality gives nonnegative cost because c belongs to I0. Thus the example respects that stronger collection of functional necessary conditions as stated.

## 4. Actual incidence and the limits of the realization

Along X(s)=(s-L,Z-s), v1 turns on at L, v2 turns off at Z, and v3 is strictly negative throughout. Every listed B point belongs to T. The x=1, y=1, and x+y=-1 support faces have positive length; P is the unique point maximizing x+y because its sum is zero and all other listed sums are negative. Thus B is a genuine polygon with the asserted supports.

The tiny F_A segment has constant x+y=51/50, larger than both other A vertex sums, and is exactly its exposed face. Its points satisfy x>-1, y<-1, x+y>1, so the strict singleton signature is correct. The other A vertices make all three specified cuts proper. The actual Minkowski face is X(I0). The extra small square has smaller (1,1) support and ensures that zero is interior to K; the full K support face is exactly X([0,1]). The arclength factors are sqrt(2) for F_K and 2sqrt(2) for F_A, producing the same common multiplier sqrt(2) in the compared costs.

These checks certify actual compatible face geometry. They do not certify the prescribed numerical section weights or global criticality, and the source says so explicitly. Thus the result is an exact obstruction to the stated functional implication, not a counterexample to a stronger actual-critical theorem or to OC.

## 5. Added actual-section refinement and two-chord area charge

The added Section 5 independently **PASSES**. Write t_i=a_i/s_i and s_i=k_i+2a_i. The independently audited actual critical chord-center inequality gives k_i>=a_i>0, hence 0<t_i<=1/3. Its exact nearer-endpoint bound is

    s_i(1-4t_i+6t_i^2)/2 <= rho_i <= s_i(1-2t_i)/2.

Both denominators are positive on the stated interval. Taking reciprocals and then applying the triangle inequality of the single actual symmetric-core gauge gives exactly (14)--(15); the normalization by Lambda is valid. Dropping the positive left denominator and bounding the j term by 3p_j gives (16). The expression under its square root is nonnegative because the same inequality forces p_l-3p_j<=3p_i. The decreasing quadratic has the asserted smaller root on [0,1/3].

For (17), the coordinate map x -> (v_i.x,v_j.x) has absolute determinant D. An actual i chord has transformed vertical length D sigma_Ai, and a j chord has transformed horizontal length D sigma_Aj. If the vertical segment straddles the horizontal line, the two triangles based on the horizontal segment have disjoint interiors and combined area LH/2. If it is on one side, its farther endpoint has distance at least H from that line. These arguments do not require the two segments to intersect. Their convex hull lies in transformed A. Dividing by D proves the stated area bound, including endpoint contact and offset chords.

For p_1=p_2=7/50 and p_3=18/25, p_3-3p_2=3/10, so (16) gives t_1,t_2>=(1-1/sqrt(5))/3. Substituting a_i=t_i/(p_i Lambda) into the determinant-one two-chord bound yields

    |A| Lambda^2 >= (1/2) [50(1-1/sqrt(5))/21]^2
                   = (1500-500sqrt(5))/441.

This is a necessary condition for an actual critical realization of those numerical weights. There is no supplied upper bound for Q Lambda^2 or any claim that the Section 4 polygons realize the weights. The source explicitly retains both limitations; the new inequality neither proves that realization impossible nor converts the functional obstruction into an actual-critical counterexample.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
